newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Anglo units buy Zambian milling company.
newsitem.headline: Anglo units buy Zambian milling company.

text.p: Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd subsidiaries, Erabas BV and Namib Milling, have bought Zambia's largest milling company in an ongoing privatisation exercise of state-run enterprises.

Anglo representative in Lusaka, Anderson Mazoka, said on Monday that the two units had bought the government's 51 percent stake in National Milling Company and taken over its liabilities of $10.6 million.

"This is a happy occasion for us as our associate company, Erabas B.V. and our technical partner, Namib Milling, take over National Milling, in keeping with the government's policy of privatisation," Mazoka said in a statement.
The new owners would invest around $2 million to improve the company's performance, which has fallen in the face of increasing local and foreign competition.
The new owners would also have to cut jobs to improve the company's performance.
Mazoka said the performance of the company, which was reaching only 45 percent of its potential annual turnover of 50 billion kwacha, was hampered by unfair trade practices in the region.
He said Zimbabwe and South Africa kept exporting cheap products to Zambia that could be produced by National Milling.
He said South Africa and Zimbabwe were able to produce such products cheaper and under COMESA, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa, they also receive rebates on taxes.
